terra.problem: The lunch comparison mentions food other than cookies.
The psalm does not say Judah was standing in a crowd of strangers.
The claim that a footstool appears elsewhere in the Bible needs a reference.
The geographical claim that the Jordan is on Israel's land goes beyond the passage and needs a reference.
The psalm does not identify the sea as the Red Sea or say that the Jordan did not change color.
The cross-examination joke makes the way the psalm is written the joke.
Calling the speaker a man assumes the unnamed writer's identity.
The joke contrasts God's act with Papa Dorin's cookie-making, rather than keeping the comparison on the human side.
The claim about altars made of stones elsewhere in Scripture needs a reference.
The psalm says God turned the rock into a pool, but does not say He did it at His word.
Judah became God's sanctuary; the psalm does not say Judah was where He made His sanctuary. It also tells the earth to tremble rather than saying the earth responded.
The psalm tells the earth to tremble; it does not say that the earth trembles.
